summary: A Sumner County lookout numbered "6-2" in Tennessee's 1976 forestry tower list; still standing, but its build year, design and staffing are unrecorded.

evidence.supports: Great Fire of 1910 motivated nationwide tower building
evidence.quote: The Great Fire of 1910, a 3-million acre wildfire in the northwest, motivated tower building across the country.

evidence.supports: CCC began building towers in 1933; ~8,000 in US by 1940
evidence.quote: The CCC in 1933 began building towers and there were about 8,000 towers in the US by 1940.

evidence.supports: Tennessee's first fire tower was at Cagle
evidence.quote: Tennessee's first fire tower was at Cagle.

evidence.supports: CCC erected 98 lookout towers in Tennessee, 1933-1941
evidence.quote: From 1933 to 1941, the Civilian Conservation Corps erected 98 lookout towers in Tennessee.

evidence.supports: table numbers are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from a 1976 list
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers.

evidence.supports: White House tower is numbered 6-2 and listed as standing
White House tower is in Sumner County at elevation 932 feet

sources.title: TN lookout tower: SRT002 White House

notes_for_editor: No source beyond tnlandforms.us mentions this specific tower by name; the register has no build year, design, agency confirmation beyond the district-tower numbering convention, staffing, or access information. Checked nhlr.org and firetower.org (FFLOS) crawl caches for Tennessee and the local raw-page caches for 'white house'/'whitehouse' — none has an entry for this tower. Two WebSearches turned up nothing tower-specific beyond tnlandforms.us. The 'agency' fact: fact-check spot-checking (2026-10-04) found the source page does directly name 'Tennessee Division of Forestry (208 tower sites c. 1976...)' alongside the district-tower numbering explanation, so this is a direct naming rather than an inference as originally noted. No corrections to the tower record are warranted — tnlandforms is already the record's source for name/location/county/elevation/status.
